More than 100 original paintings and drawings by Korean-American students from grades K to 12 will be on display at the 20th annual Korean Children’s Art Exhibit in the Courtyard of Honolulu Hale (City Hall) from June 28 to July 8, 2011.

Presented by the Korean Artists Association of Hawaii, the exhibit is part of their efforts to pave the road for future artists. The Korean Artists Association of Hawaii was established in 1986. The organization holds an annual exhibition to introduce Korean artists to the local community. Members of the organization have been recognized both nationally and internationally.

The exhibit is supported by the Mayor’s Office of Culture and the Arts. Exhibit viewing is free and open to the public, Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For more information, call the Korean Artists Association of Hawaii at 808-389-2216.

Mission Houses Museum - A National Historic Landmark.
The Mission Houses Museum connects the story of the American Protestant missionaries and their descendants to the history and culture of Hawai'i, in order to give present generations of residents and visitors a deeper understanding of, and appreciation for, Hawai'i's rich and complex history.

Come and pay us a visit at the Mission Houses Museum. You will have the opportunity to visit 3 of Hawai'i's Historical Houses built between 1821 - 1841. Go on a guided tour through these historical houses with our knowledgeable and trained docents and listen to the stories of events that occured in Hawai'i in the 19th century.

The sixth annual exhibit of The National Arts Program® in Honolulu, featuring artwork by City and County of Honolulu employees and their families, will be on display June 6 to 23, 2011, at City Hall. The exhibition is presented by The National Arts Program Foundation and the Mayor’s Office of Culture and the Arts.

City employees and their family members produced a wide variety of original paintings, drawings, photographs, sculptures, crafts and other visual art works. All works will be judged by professional arts practitioners in the following categories: amateur, intermediate, professional, and youth. Since the program began in Honolulu five years ago, City employees and their families have submitted more than 300 works for display.

The program was established in 1983 by The National Arts Program Foundation to identify the artistic talents of our nation, it involves employees and family members in more than 450 large and small cities, counties, airports, hospitals, and other organizations. The program is now producing “people’s art” at a rate of some 20,000 pieces a year. The City and County of Honolulu is currently the only organization in the state of Hawaii to participate in this program.

Exhibit viewing is free and open to the public. For more information, call the Mayor’s Office of Culture and the Arts at 808-768-6622.

BAMP Project, Hawaii's premier concert production company presents the Nas & Damian “Distant Relatives“ Hawaii tour, the first time these music icons perform side by side on stage in the islands. Unlike all previous collaborations between Jamaican and American artists, Distant Relatives is neither a remix nor a featured guest spot on a single track but a fully collaborative effort filling an entire album, opening new avenues of musical expression.

“When we first started working, I was thinking about what direction we should go in,” Nas explained during a recent discussion at the Grammy Museum. “Cause it’s all kinda like the same—reggae, rap. But it went to its own thing… We had a few concepts. All basically around empowerment in a way, cause if we’re talking about Distant Relatives we’re talking about the human family.” The sound features live musicians as well as studio production by Damian Marley and his elder brother Stephen Marley, a distinguished award-winning artist and producer in his own right. Featured artists on the album connect other diasporic dots— New Orleans’ own Lil Wayne as well as the critically acclaimed Somali-born, Canadian-raised MC K’NAAN.

The youngest son of the legendary Bob Marley, Damian “Jr. Gong” Marley garnered his own place in music history when he became the first ever reggae artist to win a Grammy Award outside of the Reggae category, taking home an award for Best Urban/Alternative performance for his smash 2005 single “Welcome To Jamrock.” The acclaimed breakthrough album of the same name also won a Grammy Award for Best Reggae Album.

A hip-hop icon since his immortal guest verse on Main Source’s 1991 “Live At The Barbeque,” Nas burst out of the Queensbridge housing projects, a hotbed of rap artistry since the early ’80s. The son of jazz trumpeter Olu Dara, Nas has since gone on to sell over 20 million albums worldwide over the span of his legendary career, and has acted as an ambassador for hip-hop culture throughout the globe.

If you are not familiar with their music please visit their website at http://www.distantrelatives.com

Diamond Head Crater Festival promoter Ron Gibson returns with a concert bill, this time away from the iconic site, as he presents the Doobie Brothers and War in concert at the Blaisdell Arena.

These two legendary bands are no strangers to Hawaii. War and founding member Lonnie Jordan were here just recently, and will be the opening band. One of the most popular groups of the 1970s, War was also one of the most eclectic bands of the time, freely melding soul, Latin, jazz and rock influences into an effortlessly funky whole.

Aside from a few years of inactivity in the mid-’80s, the Doobie Brothers have continued to perform, create and record for over 21 consecutive years. Original members Tom Johnston and Pat Simmons, joined by longtime guitarist John McFee, will lead the band through such evergreen hits as “China Grove, “Long Train Runnin’,” “Listen to the Music,” “Black Water” and “What a Fool Believes.”

Native Hawaiian Plant Society Free Public Lecture
The Native Hawaiian Plant Society will sponsor a talk titled: Working with the Plant Extinction Prevention Program (PEPP) in Hawaii and Exploring Micronesia. by Steve Pearlman of the National Tropical Botanical Gardens (NTBG), Friday, February 25th at 7pm, in the pool-side multi-purpose room of the Tavares Community Center in Pukalani, Maui. Steve will discuss his work with the Plant Extinction Prevention Program (PEP) in Hawai`i as well as his recent work in Micronesia. Steve Pearlman has been a field Botanist with the National Tropical Botanical Gardens (NTBG) for more than 33 years and has 39 years of field experience in Hawaii. He has worked with
plants on the verge of extinction throughout the South Pacific region and has pioneered botanizing cliff’s in Hawai`i using rope work.


The Native Hawaiian Plant Society (NHPS) is a volunteer-based nonprofit organization whose mission it is to preserve and restore Hawaiian native plants in their native ecosystems.

HONOLULU, HI (March 22, 2011) –Come for the baddest display of cars & motorcycles, mixed martial arts & grappling, body building fitness & figure/bikini championship, bully dog show and more at the Big Boys and MMA Hawaii Expo at the Blaisdell Exhibition Hall, scheduled for June 17, 18 and 19. “Big Boys and MMA Hawaii Expo, ‘Hawaii’s Baddest Display of Big Boys and Their Toys,’ is the premier event for men’s products, services and entertainment, but it’s not just for guys, the ladies will also be pleasantly surprised with what they can see at the event.

The event is presented by MMAhawaii.com, 2Flip Productions and HPELive, so get ready for the biggest and most exciting weekend in Hawaii culminating with Fathers Day on Sunday, June 19th, featuring dynamic sports combat, tattoo arts show, lingerie fashion show, cigar lounge and much more. No car enthusiast would want to miss out on the auto showcase, featuring the fastest cars from all around the islands. Motorcycle fans will be amazed with the finest displays of motorbike custom jobs from the most skilled in Hawaii.

Sports combat will take the spotlight with live events featuring the Hawaii Triple Crown Grappling Championships, and of course, Live MMA cage fights from UPNUP and Destiny Entertainment. The event also includes the MMA Hawaii Awards and the Miss MMA Hawaii Contest, where Hawaii’s hottest ladies, embodying both beauty and physical fitness, compete for the coveted title of Miss MMA Hawaii 2011. There will even be a Go-Go Dance Off!

Autos and sports not your thing? There’s still more for all of Hawaii’s big boys, like the best in hobbies with exhibitions including a beer garden, cigar lounge and a tech garden with all of today’s greatest gadgets. Plus, the Second Annual Hawaii's Specialty Bully Show will pit dog-against-dog and world champion big wave surfer Jamie Sterling will be on hand to sign autographs.

For the best in music, don’t miss out on our Battle of the Reggae Bands, a competition featuring local reggae talent. This monster expo will leave even the biggest of boys out of breath!

The Big Boys and MMA Hawaii Expo, ‘Hawaii’s Baddest Display of Big Boys and Their Toys’, will take the Blaisdell Exhibition Hall for a ride Friday to Sunday, June 17, 18 and 19, 2011. The Honolulu Chorale, one of Honolulu’s oldest community choruses, will present its 45th annual Spring Concert on May 8 at 4pm in the Pearl City Cultural Center. Led by music director Joseph McAlister, the group will perform Mozart’s Regina Coeli, Te Deum and delightful but rarely performed Litaniae Lauretanae. Popular Hawaiian music will include `O Makalapua, a song written especially for the Chorale by local composer Jerré Tanner. The chorale will be accompanied by the award-winning string quartet Ensemble Manoa, led by University of Hawai’i junior music major, Mai Kawahara.

Joining the Chorale in this gala concert will be the always popular Windward Choral Society, directed by Susan McCreary Duprey and performing a wide variety of ethnic based choral music.

description:
Teens, do you love to draw Anime and Manga? Show off your stuff in Liliha Public Library’s Anime Art Contest! Young adults in grades 6-12 are invited to submit artwork done in anime style. The contest is only being held at Liliha Public Library from May 15 to July 15, 2011. Winners will be announced in July 2011.

The grand prize winner will get a Manga-Comic Pro Sketching & Inking set, a red pen case, and a Canson Comic & Manga Artist Trading Cards generously donated by Sakura of America, as well as the Manga Studio Debut 4 software donated by Smith Micro Software, Inc, a Bamboo Pen donated by Wacom Technology Corporation, a set of Copic markers, and other prizes. First place winners will receive prizes that include a Pigma Sensei kit, red pen case, and a Canson Comic & Manga Artist Trading Cards, while second place winners will receive prizes that include a red pen case with a Micron pen courtesy of Sakura of America.

Winners will have their art displayed at Liliha Public Library in July. First 100 entrants will receive a free Manga instructional booklet compliments of Sakura of America. This program is funded by the Friends of Liliha Public Library, The Right Stuf International Inc., Sakura of America, Smith Micro Software Inc. and Wacom Technology Corporation.

For official contest rules, an entry form, or for more information, visit the Liliha Public Library or call 587-7577.

Touched by the devastating images and stories of survival in the wake of the March 11 Japan disaster, Haseko Hawaii, Inc. and Hoakalei Charities will host a Friendship Golf Tournament on Friday, May 6, 2011, at the Ernie-Els designed golf course at Hoakalei Country Club. The 18-hole tournament will benefit the Japanese Red Cross Society and all proceeds will go toward their disaster relief efforts.

Registration will begin at 10:30 a.m., followed by a shotgun start at 12 noon. The format is a 3 Man Team Scramble. Golfers will enjoy hosted lunch and drinks during play, an awards ceremony with door prize giveaways, and a banquet to follow.

The entry deadline is April 29, 2011. Volunteer positions are open to those who wish to help in other ways and prize donations will also be accepted for the ceremony.

Hospice Hawaii will host its annual Family Bereavement Camp Ka Pilina Pulama at the Queen Liliuokalani Children’s Center in Punaluu. The camp is for families with children 7-17 years old who have lost a loved one to death in the past three to four years. The camp provides a balance of fun activities and introspective exercises to assist families with the process of loss, grief, remembrance and healing.

The deadline to apply is April 30, 2011.
